post.title: Friday night dinner ride
post.body:
Friday night, my wife and I decided dinner was worth riding to. Helmets on, across the main road and up a back way that's more dirt than road, a bit bumpy and a lot more fun than driving.

## The stop for the sky

A few minutes in I stopped for the sky. Over the ridge there was a cloud with a rainbow running through it, pink, green and violet like oil on water.

> Over the ridge there was a cloud with a rainbow running through it, pink, green and violet like oil on water.

## No lights

Ordering went fine. Then we realized neither of us had brought a bike light, and the sun was already heading behind the Sierra. Dinner to go, and home the long way on the best-lit roads we know.

## The long way home

The sky made up for it on the way back: a long pink streak over the mountains and the sagebrush going dark below it.

What I learned: pack the lights, even for a ride to dinner.

episode.title: Pack the lights
episode.script:
It was a Friday evening in early October, a little after six, when Christian and Ha-Leen-Ah made a decision. Tonight, dinner would be reached by bike.

Helmets on. Out across the main road, then up a back way that was more dirt than road. Bumpy. A little more off-road than two people need on their way to eat. Nobody minded. That was half the fun.

***

A few minutes in, Christian looked up and stopped.

Over the dark ridge of the mountains, a cloud was doing something clouds rarely do. Pale gold at the edges, and through the middle, a smear of every color. Pink, green, violet, running together like oil on water. A rainbow, folded right into a cloud.

He took three pictures. Then they rode on.

***

Dinner was the easy part. The ordering went smoothly. And that's when they noticed what they didn't have.

Lights.

The sun was already heading down behind the Sierra, and neither of them had brought a bike light. I'm not saying whose job the lights were. So, a new plan. Dinner to go, and a ride home on the best-lit roads they knew, instead of the bumpy way they came. Sensible.

***

And on the way back, the sky put on a second show. The sagebrush went dark and quiet. Behind the mountains, the light turned cream, then pink, one long streak of it across the sky, glowing at the edges of the ridge.

Christian stopped once more for that. Wouldn't you?

***

They made it home safe, in the last of the light. And a few minutes later they were sitting down to a hot dinner, earned the long way around.

The lesson was noted. Again. Pack the lights, even for dinner.
